reference: Martin & Moyce (1952) dam-break front trajectory — independent transcription used as a cross-check
role: cross-check only: never a validation gate. It exists so the uncertainty of the bundled table can be *measured* instead of assumed.

source.paper: Martin, J.C. & Moyce, W.J. (1952). An experimental study of the collapse of liquid columns on a rigid horizontal plane. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences, 244(882), 312-324.
source.digitisation_origin: Value-identical with the digitisation distributed inside Lethe's official dam-break post-processing (LETE-CFD/lethe, dam-break Martin & Moyce example).
source.transcription_path: Transcribed from the frozen anchor table of the sibling solver workspace: m9/benchmarks/pending/dam_break_sc/result.json, key `reference_digitisation_lethe` (14 points). Verified at transcription time by comparing the 14 (T, Z) pairs element by element.
source.caveat: Neither this table nor the bundled one has been checked against the archived paper text: the 1952 paper is paywalled and figure-level digitisation is the only access route. The two tables are independent transcriptions of the same figure, so their spread is a *lower bound* on the reference uncertainty, not a measurement of it.

convention.dependent_variable: X = x_front / a. The front is measured from the wall, so the initial column edge sits at X = 1 and Z/a = X - 1. The bundled table reports Z/a directly, so the two are compared after removing the offset 1.
convention.aspect_ratio: column height / width = 2, matching the bundled table and the case configuration in src/tensorsph/dam_break.py
